jobs.title: Warehouse Data Analyst
jobs.description:
*Turn warehouse data into the decisions that keep high-tech supply chains moving.* ***This position is based in Virginia and is NOT REMOTE***

The Dulles corridor runs on data. From the data centers of Loudoun County to the air cargo moving through Dulles Airport, this region is where logistics and technology meet, and this role sits right at that intersection.

At Arnoff, our partner Dulles facility supports a forward stocking location for a leading technology customer, where the right part in the right place at the right time really matters. We are looking for a Warehouse Data Analyst who loves clean numbers, sharp reports, and finding the story hiding in a spreadsheet. You will be the person that we rely on to know exactly what is on hand, what shipped, and how we are performing.

WHY YOU'LL LOVE THIS ROLE

* **Real impact, fast. Your reports go straight to program managers, supervisors, and Finance, and they drive daily decisions, customer scorecards, and billing.**
* **Room to build.** We want recurring reports to be automated. If you like that automation, you will have a real playground to put it to work.
* **Be the go-to person.** You will serve as Arnoff's representative and main point of contact at the facility, and you will train teammates on our reports and systems.
* **Learn the whole operation.** You will get hands-on with the warehouse floor so your analysis is grounded in how the work actually happens, which is great experience for a career in supply chain analytics or program management.
* **A schedule that fits life.** Weekday daytime hours with overtime eligibility, in a location that is easy to reach from Loudoun, western Fairfax, and the Route 28 corridor.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own the reporting rhythm

* Run and distribute assigned reports, including on-hand inventory and requested transactional reports.
* Run the shipment and location reports that set the Supervisor up for the day.
* Compile and enter milestone data for the daily milk run.
* Prepare weekly and monthly cycle count reports for the Program Manager.

Power the numbers that matter

* Build the data behind scorecard updates and KPI, SLA, volume, and spend reporting.
* Provide billing data to the Program Manager and Finance every billing cycle.
* Supply controllable-error data to support warehouse performance reviews.
* Spot data discrepancies and flag them to the Supervisor for correction.

Make it better

* Automate recurring reports and keep report documentation current.
* Train staff on reports and system use.
* Serve as Arnoff's main point of contact at the facility and support project management as needed.

WHAT YOU BRING

* A bachelor's degree in analytics, supply chain, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 2+ years in reporting or analytics, ideally in warehousing or logistics.
* Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, Power Query, lookups). Power BI or Tableau is a big plus.
* Experience pulling and reconciling data from existing systems.
* A working understanding of inventory concepts like shrinkage, cycle counts and on-hand buckets.
* Clear, accurate writing that turns findings into actionable insights.

Bonus points if: you have military logistics, supply, or 3PL experience, or you are the kind of person who can't leave a broken formula alone.

THE DETAILS

Location

On-site in Dulles, VA, close to Route 28, the Dulles Toll Road, and Washington Dulles International Airport

Schedule

Weekdays, 8:00 am – 5:00 pm (40 hours, with a 1-hour unpaid lunch). No nights, no weekends.

Pay type

Hourly, overtime-eligible (non-exempt)

Pay range

$32 - $36 per Hour

Reports to

Applied Program Manager

READY TO MAKE THE NUMBERS MOVE?

If you are detail-driven, curious, and ready to be the data backbone of a busy, high-tech operation, we would love to hear from you.

Benefits:

  

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

**Description**

**Who is USP?**

The U.S. Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) is an independent scientific organization that collaborates with the world’s leading health and science experts to develop rigorous quality standards for medicines, dietary supplements, and food ingredients. At USP, we believe that scientific excellence is driven by a commitment to fairness, integrity, and global collaboration. This belief is embedded in our core value of Passion for Quality and is demonstrated through the contributions of more than 1,300 professionals across twenty global locations, working to strengthen the supply of safe, high-quality medicines worldwide.

At USP, we value inclusive scientific collaboration and recognize that attracting diverse expertise strengthens our ability to develop trusted public health standards. We foster an organizational culture that supports equitable access to mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Our partnerships, standards, and research reflect our belief that ensuring broad participation in scientific leadership results in stronger, more impactful outcomes for global health.

USP is proud to be an equal employment opportunity employer (EEOE) and is committed to ensuring fair, merit-based selection processes that enable the best scientific minds—regardless of background—to contribute to advancing public health solutions worldwide. We provide reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities and uphold policies that create an inclusive and collaborative work environment.

**Brief Job Overview**

The Associate Program Analyst serves as a key operational and programmatic partner to the Director and Equity Office team, supporting the implementation of the Equity Equals Excellence Strategy through project coordination, stakeholder engagement, research, communications, data analysis, and operational support. **How will YOU create impact here at USP?**

Additionally, USP’s People and Culture division, in partnership with the Equity Office, invests in leadership and workforce development to equip all employees with the skills to create high-performing, inclusive teams. This includes training in equitable management practices and tools to promote engaged, collaborative, and results-driven work environments.

**Entity:**

**Job Description:**

**About bp**
------------

**Our purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. For over 100 years, bp has focused on discovering, developing, and producing oil and gas in the nations where we operate. We are one of the few companies globally that can provide governments and customers with an integrated energy offering. Delivering our strategy sustainably is fundamental to achieving our ambition to be a net zero company by 2050 or sooner!**

  
  

**You will work with:**

The Transformation, Analytics and Insights (TAI) team reports directly to the EVP Technology and is distributed globally across US, UK, India and Malaysia. We work to ensure that Technology is an efficient, effective and trusted partner for the bp business. Our activities span from creating tooling to support improved delivery efficiency to supporting transformation activity and mergers & acquisitions. We are tightly coupled across the team to Technology leadership and highly visible within the Technology organization.

Ways of working within the TAI team is a team of trusted advisors working alongside SVPs and VPs to deliver changes to working practices and embedding transformation change. We act as a consultancy, providing short engagements with longer term governance to ensure that initiatives are embedded that may be devised by the wider TAI team utilising a fail fast and scale mental model. We problem solve for our SVPs and VPs, demonstrating deep relationships across the TAI team and Technology. The pace is fast and changable; we care deeply about each other, are kind even when it is tough to speak the truth and have each other’s back.

  
  

**Let me tell you about the role**
----------------------------------

Project Managers skillfully balance constraints, manage team members and interdependencies, mitigate risks, and resolve conflicting priorities to deliver successful outcomes. Change managers drive the success of large-scale transformations by ensuring that the organization is equipped to embrace new ways of working. This role is a hybrid of project and change management due to the work undertaken by the team. You will play a critical part in enabling teams to adapt to shifts in structure, processes, and tools, aligning team members around a shared vision for change and creating strategies and roadmaps that add clarity and focus. By fostering engagement, building trust, and creating conditions for sustained adoption, you will accelerate the realization of business value and positions the organization for long-term success in a dynamic, global environment.

  
  

**What you will deliver**
-------------------------

**Knowledge and Change Document Support**: Coordinate across multiple teams to pull together coherent documents to support change. Create user journeys, task flows, and service blueprints that clarify how users interact with the content. Support teams in creating useful, well thought out content.

**Change management Support:** Provide support on org design activities within the team, where needed conduct data analysis and manage project timelines.

**Project and programme management**: Support the development and implementation of detailed project plans, including schedules, budgets, resource allocation, and delivery roadmaps. Use appropriate methodologies to deliver projects on time, within budget, and at the desired quality. Coordinate across teams to ensure project alignment with bp’s strategic objectives.

**Engagement and training:** Support the delivery of sophisticated cross-functional engagement plans and global multi-channel communication campaigns to drive awareness and adoption. Support the definition and implementation of training approaches for new processes, platforms, products, and features to ensure teams are well-prepared and confident in new ways of working.

**Metrics and analytics:** Identify, develop, implement and track metrics that measure the impact of change, for use in understanding performance against targets, industry peers, competitors and objectives.

**AI-assisted exploration:** Use AI tools appropriate to support early exploration, content refinement, or research synthesis while ensuring human review and responsible use.

  
  

**What you will need to be successful (experience and qualifications)**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Required

* Strong problem-solving and critical thinking with the ability to think strategically and make data-driven decisions.
* Strong communication with the ability to articulate complex ideas clearly and effectively verbally and in writing
* Strong relationship skills, able to motivate cross-functional teams.
* Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.
* Curiosity to learn and adopt emerging tools and technologies including Figma Make, Loveable, Claude, SharePoint, Confluence and AI-enabled workflows.
* Experience with digital tools and technology for metrics and analytics.

**Desirable**
-------------

* Experience in leading or supporting change management initiatives, preferably within a global organization.
* Understanding of change management principles, methodologies, and tools.
* Experience in developing and implement effective training programs.
* Qualifications in Agile delivery, change management or product management
* Experience in working with senior partners (VP and above) to deliver change

At this level, the Project Manager has basic proficiency in independently handling a range of basic tasks. They complete tasks with general supervision, balancing priorities, monitoring progress, and resolving straightforward issues. Partner management and systems development skills are strengthening, as they begin to coordinate with broader teams and refine delivery techniques. While gaining experience in organizational change, they focus on supporting the team.

**Department:** Fraud and Security

**Team:** *T-ISAC*

**Location:** *London with hybrid ways of working*

**What the hiring manager says**

*The GSMA is expanding the T-ISAC Team and looking for a candidate with a passion to provide intelligence analytical expertise that will provide unrivalled value to our mobile network operators. If you have proven experience in finding the truth behind the noise and can articulate the ‘So What’ to senior telecoms defence specialists across the disciplines of cyber, networking and fraud / scams, you would be welcome to join GSMA T-ISAC and help make a real-world difference to combat our adversaries.*

***Matthew Roach, T-ISAC Engagement Manager***

**About the Team & T-ISAC**

The GSMA is at the heart of the modern mobile communications ecosystem. These systems are rightly considered critical to national infrastructure, and our members defend themselves and their consumers from cyber, networking and fraud / scam attacks every minute of every day.

The T-ISAC team brings together the defence analysts from across the mobile world to share intelligence and produce actionable, timely and relevant outputs that help ensure the resilience and operational strength of our communication infrastructure. We believe that threat detection from one mobile network operator should serve to help to better defend industry peers and consumers.

  

The Telecommunication Information Sharing and Analysis Center (T-ISAC) is the cybersecurity threat intelligence community for the telecommunication industry, dedicated to facilitating collaboration and intelligence sharing among mobile network operators, mobile virtual network operators and industry stakeholders. T-ISAC provides GSMA members with critical cyber threat intelligence, fostering a trusted environment where telecommunication stakeholders can proactively address cybersecurity threats and reduce risks through the development of best practices. By uniting telecommunication MNOs, MVNOs, manufacturers, service providers and industry in a shared mission, T-ISAC enhances the mobile ecosystem’s resilience against cyber threats. For more information, visit www.gsma.com/T-ISAC.

**About the role**

As the Security Analyst (T-ISAC) you will be driving T-ISAC threat intel sharing platform’s day-to-day, combining sensitive source data with open-source insights and telecoms professional knowledge from the wider telecoms and cyber security community to facilitate intelligence exchange, capture emerging attack trends and translate insights into actionable intelligence for strategic decision-makers. The role will analyse data across T-ISAC’s intelligence platforms to identify thematic threats to global mobile networks and consumers, while supporting sector-wide incident coordination, information sharing, threat monitoring and resilience activities.

Working independently and as part of a small team, as the Analyst you will collaborate with internal teams, subject matter experts and leadership to deliver strategic initiatives aligned with organisational priorities and T-ISAC member needs. Drawing on a detailed understanding of attacker tools, techniques and procedures, threat actor behaviour and the cyber, network and fraud landscape, the role will produce high-quality intelligence products and clearly translate technical indicators, methodologies and potential impacts for both specialist and business audiences.

**About You**

Within T-ISAC, you will gain global visibility of the threats facing the mobile network providers. You will use your strategic report writing abilities to convey valuable intelligence and industry-wide insights, detailing of the threat landscape to key strategic decision makers and budget holders.

You have an understanding of the fundamentals of telecoms network security and defence across SS7, Diameter and GTP-C using signalling firewalls and intrusion detection systems.

You will need to have practitioner-level ability in suing MISP and other telecoms security tools, as well as basic coding ability in Python, Linux and building API integration to enable data exchange.

You are a big-picture thinker with a strong analytical mindset and hand-on experience in high performing analytical teams, ideally with a telecoms background.

You are mindful of geo-political impact and the motivations of adversaries as they carry out attacks across or directed at mobile networks.

You are self-motivated and highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to independently manage responsibilities and deliver results.

jobs.description:
**Job overview**

The Cyber Security Manager is responsible for leading the Trust’s operational cyber security function and providing expert advice, assurance and guidance to support safe, resilient and secure digital services across The Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust.

The postholder will lead on the development, implementation and continual improvement of cyber security controls, processes and governance arrangements to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the Trust’s systems, infrastructure, applications and information assets.

The postholder will provide specialist leadership across cyber risk management, security operations, incident response, vulnerability management, assurance, awareness and policy development.

They will work closely with Digital, Information Governance, clinical and operational services, third-party suppliers and external partners to ensure the Trust meets relevant statutory, regulatory and NHS cyber security requirements, including the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT), Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF), Cyber Essentials and other recognised standards and good practice.

The role will also support senior governance arrangements by providing timely reporting, assurance and expert advice to relevant Trust committees and senior leads on cyber risk, incidents, compliance and resilience.

The postholder will play a key role in shaping and delivering the Trust’s cyber security strategy and roadmap, helping to set priorities, inform investment planning, funding bids and assurance activity, and ensure that local cyber security plans align with organisational objectives, digital transformation, and relevant national and regional cyber security strategies, frameworks and priorities.

**Main duties of the job**

The postholder will lead and manage the delivery of cyber security services and improvement activity across the Trust, ensuring a proactive, risk-based and intelligence-led approach to cyber resilience.

The role will require the postholder to work with senior stakeholders, provide expert advice on complex technical and governance matters, and influence decisions that support the protection of patient care, business continuity and organisational reputation.

The postholder will be expected to provide visible leadership for cyber security across the Trust, support the Infrastructure Manager with strategic planning and assurance, and take responsibility for the delivery and performance of assigned staff, services and work programmes.

The Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust (PAHT) is proud to care for the communities of West Essex, delivering safe, compassionate, and high-quality services. We are part of the Neighbourhood Wavea national programme that’s changing how care is delivered by focusing on prevention, early support, and more joined-up services across health, social care, and the voluntary sector.

This means we’re working more closely with local partners to bring care closer to home and support people to live healthier, more independent lives.

We’re a supportive and inclusive organisation that values its people. We offer development opportunities, flexible working, and a strong focus on wellbeing. As a Disability Confident and equal opportunities employer, we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences.

Join us and help shape the future of care in West Essex.

**Detailed job description and main responsibilities**

Key duties and responsibilities include:

Lead the day-to-day management and continual improvement of the Trust’s cyber security capability, including processes, technologies, controls, procedures and associated documentation.

Develop, implement and maintain cyber security policies, standards, procedures and guidance that support the Trust’s strategic objectives, statutory obligations and national NHS requirements.

Provide expert cyber security advice to senior managers, Digital colleagues, programme teams, clinical services and corporate functions on risk, assurance, control design and secure implementation of new and existing technologies, including cloud services and hybrid environments.

Lead the identification, assessment, prioritisation and treatment of cyber security risks, ensuring risks are clearly articulated, documented, escalated and monitored through appropriate governance routes.

Provide assurance, reporting and expert advice to senior governance groups and designated leads on cyber security risk, incidents, control effectiveness and compliance activity.

Oversee vulnerability management processes, including scanning, assessment, remediation planning, exception handling and reporting, working with infrastructure, applications and third-party suppliers to reduce cyber risk.

Lead the Trust’s response to cyber security incidents and events, coordinating investigation, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned and follow-up actions, and participate in the Trust’s on-call rota to provide out-of-hours support for cyber security incidents, major incidents and urgent service issues as required.

Ensure appropriate monitoring, alerting, triage and escalation arrangements are in place for cyber security events, and that security tools such as SIEM, endpoint protection, email security and privileged access controls are configured and used effectively to support detection, response and assurance.

Lead on cyber assurance activity, including preparing evidence, coordinating responses and supporting the completion of the Data Security and Protection Toolkit, Cyber Assessment Framework requirements, audits and external reviews including penetration testing.

Support the development and testing of cyber resilience, business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements, including leading tabletop exercises, incident simulations and post-incident reviews.

Work with infrastructure, applications, suppliers and service owners to support high availability, service uptime and operation

The senior IT project manager will lead the successful delivery of oracle finance, project financial management and HCM capabilities, ensuring the programme delivers measurable business outcomes, operational improvements and sustainable value.

The role is accountable for end-to-end programme delivery, from mobilisation through design, build, testing, deployment, hyper care and benefits realisation. Working alongside business sponsors, technology teams and implementation partners, the role will ensure that Oracle capabilities are deployed in a way that supports Mace's global operating model, governance requirements and growth ambitions.

**You’ll be responsible for:**
  
  
**Programme delivery and leadership**

* Directing the end-to-end delivery of oracle fusion cloud finance, project financial management and HCM programmes across Mace Consult.
* Own programme scope, schedule, budget, quality, resources and benefits throughout the delivery lifecycle.
* Develop and maintain integrated programme plans covering business, technology, data, testing, change and deployment activities.
* Manage critical dependencies, risks, issues and decision points across multiple workstreams.
* Deliver programme outcomes aligned to agreed business objectives, success criteria and executive expectations.

**Oracle finance and project financial management**

* Lead delivery of oracle fusion financials including general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, cash management and financial reporting.
* Lead delivery of oracle project financial management capabilities, supporting Mace's project-based revenue and cost management model.
* Work with finance leadership to standardise financial processes, controls and reporting across legal entities and geographies.
* Ensure readiness for period end close, statutory reporting, audit requirements and financial controls.

**Oracle HCM**

* Lead delivery of Oracle HCM capabilities including core hr, absence management, time and labour, talent management and workforce reporting.
* Partner with HR/TA leadership to standardise and optimise hire-to-retire processes across global operations.
* Ensure workforce and organisational data are effectively migrated and managed.
* Support regulatory and compliance requirements across all operating regions.

**Business transformation and process improvement**

* Drive business-led transformation rather than technology deployment alone.
* Facilitate process redesign workshops and challenge non-standard requirements where Oracle best practice provides a suitable alternative.
* Promote standardisation, simplification and automation of business processes.
* Ensure alignment between finance, HR, projects, procurement and enterprise reporting processes.

**Governance and stakeholder management**

* Establish and maintain effective programme governance and reporting structures.
* Lead steering committees, programme reviews and executive reporting forums.
* Maintain programme RAID logs, dependency management and decision registers.
* Manage formal change control processes for scope, budget, resources and timelines.
* Influence senior stakeholders across finance, HR, technology and executive leadership teams.

**Third-party and vendor management**

* Manage Oracle implementation partners and third-party delivery teams.
* Oversee statements of Work, delivery milestones, commercial performance and contractual obligations.
* Hold delivery partners accountable for quality, schedule, resource commitments and programme outcomes.
* Ensure effective collaboration between internal teams and external suppliers.

**Data, integration and testing**

* Oversee data migration strategy, execution and quality management activities.
* Lead integration delivery including Oracle integration cloud and associated enterprise interfaces.
* Ensure successful planning and execution of system integration testing, user acceptance testing, payroll validation, finance close rehearsals and cutover rehearsals.
* Define and manage go live readiness criteria and deployment approvals.

**Business readiness and adoption**

* Lead organisational readiness, communications, stakeholder engagement and training activities.
* Ensure business ownership of processes, controls, data and benefit realisation.
* Manage cutover, hyper care and transition into operational support.
* Ensure successful adoption of new processes and ways of working.

**Benefits realisation**

* Develop and maintain the programme business case and benefits register.
* Track and report realised benefits against agreed targets.
* Ensure benefits have clear ownership, measurement criteria and realisation plans.
* Focus benefits on value creation including operational efficiency, working capital improvement, compliance, control enhancement and employee experience.

**You’ll need to have****:**

* Significant experience delivering enterprise ERP, finance or HCM transformation programmes.
* Minimum three full lifecycle Oracle Cloud implementations in a senior delivery role.
* Experience delivering Oracle fusion financials and Oracle HCM programmes.
* Experience managing programmes valued at £5m+.
* Experience operating within complex, multi-entity and multi-country environments.
* Strong experience managing systems integrators and third-party delivery partners.
* Demonstrable experience engaging executive stakeholders at CFO, CHRO and CIO/CDIO level.
* Proven experience managing programme risks, governance, budget and benefits realisation.
* Desirable
* Oracle cloud certifications in financials, HCM or implement

Our world-leading Time & Frequency department is seeking a **Service Operations Analyst** with proven expertise in **IT service management (ITSM).**

This is an exceptional opportunity to join the global authority in **precision timing** at a defining moment for UK digital infrastructure.

Backed by a government investment of £180 million in the National Timing Centre (NTC) programme, we are developing a world-first resilient time distribution capability that will provide industry with a robust complement to satellite systems (such as GPS) – which are increasingly vulnerable to disruption from solar storms, jamming and spoofing.

This will underpin essential services, including:

* Telecommunications,
* Online banking,
* Emergency response,
* Transport networks, and
* Wider digital and data-driven operations.

Together, these services form the backbone of modern society - and your leadership will help ensure they remain secure, reliable and robust even if global navigation satellite systems fail.

* **Lead Change Enablement activities**, ensuring requests are appropriately assessed, reviewed and implemented.

jobs.title: Transaction Reporting Business Analyst/Project Manager
jobs.description:
**About Northern Trust**

As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions.

  

Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide.

  

With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service.

  
  

As a Transaction Reporting Business Analyst / Project Manager, you will play a critical role in supporting the strategic direction and development of our products and solutions for Trade and Transaction Reporting.

You will work closely with Tech, Operations, Compliance, Legal and Front Office and be responsible for managing multiple streams of work and translate regulator guidance in business and functional requirements, agree the testing approach and follow end to end delivery.

Major duties include:

  

**Business Analysis**: conduct thorough evaluations of the regulatory guidance with the goal of understanding the impact on business and operations and to create business and functional requirements for Trade and Transaction Reporting projects.

  

**Project Management**: coordinate with the portfolio change lead as well as several teams to ensure consistent business practices and create planning artefacts and coordinate project activities. Regularly communicate project status, progress and updates to virtual team and any other stakeholders, through defined standard processes and ad hoc, as needed.

  

**Testing**: coordinate and support when the testing team to ensure smooth completion of UAT and Production Parallel phases.

  

The ideal candidate should have a fair amount of the following skills & experience:

  

* Requires significant experience in project & program management and change initiatives; covering such areas as product development, regulatory change, technical transformation, and operational efficiencies. A proven track record of success managing programs/projects in a fast-paced environment with challenging deadlines, multiple priorities and limited resources.
* Proven experience in driving change in Capital Markets and particularly Transaction Reporting both as a project manager and a business analyst.
* Ability to translate regulatory text into implementation requirements and interface with Tech, Operations, Compliance, Legal and Front Office teams to understand the impact.
* Genuine curiosity in tracing data back to the golden source and design mapping to regulatory schema.
* Confident in managing complex transformation from requirement definition, new controls identification to testing and rollout.
* Must have strong organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills to manage complex projects.
* Requires excellent communication skills (both written and oral)
* Demonstrate ability to quickly establish credibility and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Highly flexible and adaptable to change.
* PMI Certifications (PMP, PRINCE2) is highly recommended, but not required.
Agile certifications and/or experience in executing in Agile Scrum methodology a plus.  

  

**Work Authorization**

Applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. This includes Skilled Worker visas, Global Business Mobility routes, Graduate visas, Youth Mobility Scheme, High Potential Individual visas, Scale-up Worker visas, Temporary Worker visas, and other employer-sponsored visa categories.

**Working with Us**

As a Northern Trust partner, you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture, which has a strong history of financial strength and stability. Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve.

jobs.title: Insider Threat Program Analyst
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

**INSIDER THREAT PROGRAM ANALYST**

SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world's most advanced technologies including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we are a target of adversaries, both foreign and domestic, focused on slowing us down and accessing our proprietary technology. The work we do will literally safeguard mankind becoming an interplanetary species.

You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the safety and security of personnel, brand, global assets, intellectual property, and operations at SpaceX. This role will triage anomalous event data and analyze insider threat program datasets to respond to threats posed to SpaceX. You will use comprehensive understanding of various collection methods and platforms to explore new data sources, build effective queries, and combine information from disparate sources.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Conduct comprehensive investigations and analysis in support of SpaceX intellectual property and security
* Uphold investigation and analytic tradecraft standards including confidentiality, objectivity, lawfulness, timeliness, and use of all available sources of information
* Collect and analyze available program data to evaluate insider threat risk to SpaceX infrastructure, programs, and operations
* Triage anomalous event data associated with indicators of data exfiltration, data destruction and other key indicators of concern
* Conduct internal investigations working with Information Security, HR, Legal, Government Security, Physical Security, and external partners based on information derived from internal and external sources
* Utilize network monitoring, data analytic, and other tools (DLP/SIEM/UEBA) to identify anomalous activity, initiate investigations and decipher underlying trends
* Extract and organize insider threat program data to build metrics, reports and case studies addressing mission requirements and timelines
* Communicate findings in a timely and accurate manner to team members, management, and relevant stakeholders
* Support employee training and briefings for internal and external audiences
* Liaise with external industry and government partners to benchmark insider threat program, share threat intelligence, and further investigations
* Continuously identify and help implement program improvement methods
* Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case files, employee PII, and intelligence reports

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in internal investigations, information security, or counterintelligence; OR 4+ years professional experience in information security, internal investigations, or counterintelligence in lieu of a degree

**PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:**

* 1+ year using a SIEM and/or conducting digital forensic investigations in a government or corporate environment
* Working level understanding of insider threat program missions, internal stakeholders, and manifestations of insider threats
* Proficiency in Microsoft Purview for eDiscovery
* Experience performing business process automation or constructing data pipelines
* Familiarity with risk-based alerting, detection, and tuning concepts for insider risk
* Experience conducting preliminary assessments, determining scope, investigation planning, evidence collection/handling, interviewing and reporting findings to internal and external stakeholders
* Ability to conduct interviews on short notice according to established internal guidelines.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise reports
* Highly organized with a strong attention to detail
* Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines
* Can swiftly adapt to new technical environments and workflows
* Ability to exercise discretion when conducting confidential investigations

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations
* Must be willing to travel ad hoc
* Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:**  
  
Pay Range:  
Level 1: $85,000 - $110,000  
Level 2: $100,000 - $135,000

  

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. **DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Application deadline: Oct 19, 2026  
  
A typical day centers on keeping the Food Safety Audits programs running smoothly and the 3P auditor relationship healthy and productive. The Program Manager II leads the Worldwide Grocery Stores retail food safety audit program, partnering with a third party audit vendor, food safety analysts, store leadership, and cross functional stakeholders to ensure compliance with FDA Food Code.
  
  
Key job responsibilities  
The role requires a results-oriented, analytical, customer-service approach to manage the audit program, measure progress, and drive risk management and compliance outcomes.

* Own accountability to the 3P Food Safety Auditor’s KPI scorecard; monitor audit completion, on-time delivery, scoring consistency, and finding-closure metrics, and act to keep them on target.
* Manage the relationship with the 3P audit provider — align on audit standards and expectations, resolve data and scoring discrepancies, and hold the provider to KPI commitments.
* Analyze and trend large audit data sets from internal and external audits to identify emerging Food Safety risks, recurring violations, and improvement opportunities.
* Verify Food Safety policy and the FDA Food Code are correctly reflected in audit standards, checklists, and scoring criteria.
* Support Food Safety escalations arising from audits; track corrective and preventive actions to closure with Operations stakeholders.
* Optimize audit procedures, processes, and best practices to improve efficiency, data quality, and reporting cycle time.
* Anticipate near-term bottlenecks in the audit program; identify, track, and mitigate immediate issues and risks, escalating when appropriate.

* 3+ years of driving process improvements experience

Since our founding in 1986, we have graded and authenticated millions of items. We employ more than 3000 people across our headquarters in Santa Ana, California and offices in New Jersey, Texas, Florida, Japan, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the UK, and France.

jobs.description:
General Statement of Job:

The Senior Information Security Analyst is a senior individual contributor responsible for advancing SIS's information security program and for leading the company's effort to achieve and maintain ISO 27001 certification. This individual owns the day-to-day operation of the Information Security Management System (ISMS)—risk assessment, control implementation, policy development, internal audit readiness, and evidence collection—and serves as the primary respondent to client cyber security surveys, questionnaires, and third-party assessments. The role is measured by steady, incremental progress against SIS's published security objectives across the cloud, identity, endpoint, and network environment, as well as the physical security technologies deployed at SIS offices and at client sites monitored by the Fusion Center. SIS operates a predominantly Apple environment (approximately 90% macOS) supporting a 24/7 Global Security Operations Center. The Senior Information Security Analyst works within an ITIL-based operational framework and reports directly to the Director of Technology.

This is an individual contributor role without direct reports. The Senior Information Security Analyst operates as a peer to the Senior Manager of IT Infrastructure and Senior Manager of Applications and works closely with the IT Infrastructure, Applications, Help Desk, and Fusion Center teams to implement and validate security controls across the enterprise. The position carries functional authority for security requirements and compliance obligations, influencing technical direction through subject matter expertise rather than direct supervision.

Essential Job Functions:

* Design and maintain security reference architectures and technical security standards across the cloud, identity, endpoint, network, application, and physical security domains, and review proposed designs and infrastructure changes against them (15%)
* Administer, tune, and monitor security tooling in partnership with the Senior Cloud Administrator, including endpoint detection and response (SentinelOne), vulnerability management, email security, data protection, and a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) solution, ensuring alerts are actionable and triaged (10%)
* Own vulnerability management and remediation across endpoints, infrastructure, and cloud services, including patch currency, device encryption, configuration hardening, and periodic least-privilege access reviews (10%)
* Build and automate security operations through scripting and platform integration, including continuous control monitoring, automated evidence collection, access review workflows, and alert enrichment, reducing reliance on manual, point-in-time compliance effort (10%)
* Support security incident response, including investigation, containment coordination, documentation, root cause analysis, and post-incident reporting, working closely with IT Infrastructure and Fusion Center leadership (5%)
* Conduct security reviews of enterprise business applications, including Salesforce, Sage Intacct, the enterprise workforce management platform, and internally developed applications, covering role and permission models, segregation of duties, data sharing and export controls, API and integration credentials, audit logging, and data retention (5%)
* Establish secure development and application security requirements for custom and client-facing applications, including secure coding standards, dependency and vulnerability scanning, penetration testing cadence, and remediation tracking with internal development and vendor teams (5%)
* Drive onboarding of enterprise applications to centralized identity, including Single Sign-On and automated provisioning, and conduct periodic application-level access reviews and offboarding validation (2%)
* Contribute information security and technical expertise to the standards and longer-term strategy for physical security technologies in use at SIS offices and at client sites monitored by the Fusion Center, including video management and camera platforms, access control and badge systems, and emerging AI-based detection and video analytics capabilities, in partnership with the Director of Technology, Fusion Center leadership, and other system owners (5%)
* Ensure physical security systems are deployed and maintained in line with information security requirements, including network segmentation, device hardening, credential and certificate management, firmware currency, centralized logging, and data retention and privacy obligations (5%)
* Perform security review of new technologies, vendors, and contracts, including third-party risk assessment and review of security exhibits and data protection terms (3%)
* Lead SIS's ISO 27001 certification effort end to end, including scoping and the Statement of Applicability, gap assessment against Annex A controls, hands-on implementation and configuration of the technical controls, internal audit, remediation of findings, and successful completion of the Stage 1 and Stage 2 certification audits (TEMPORARY, FIRST ~8 MONTHS)
* Operate and mature the Information Security Management System on an ongoing basis, maintaining the risk register and risk treatment plans, coordinating management review, tracking corrective actions, and preparing the organization for annual surveillance audits and recertification (5%)
* Serve as the primary respondent for client cyber security surveys, security questionnaires, and third-party risk assessments (for example, CAIQ, SIG, and custom client formats), maintaining a curated answer library and evidence repository, and converting identified gaps and client commitments into tracked remediation items driven to closure with the responsible technical owners (5%)
* Define, measure, and report on SIS's security objectives and key security metrics, delivering visible incremental improvement quarter over quarter and reporting progress to tech

Ø Strong documentation, communication, and organisational skills

**We Offer:**

jobs.description:
**Background**

The California Institute for Regenerative Medicine (CIRM) is a state agency created by California voters to accelerate stem cell and gene therapies for people with unmet medical needs. Since 2004, Californians have entrusted CIRM with $8.5 billion to accelerate promising discoveries through clinical trials, train a regenerative medicine workforce, strengthen the state’s biotechnology economy, and expand access to transformative treatments. Today, CIRM is pioneering new models of therapy development and accelerating medical breakthroughs that change lives, in California and around the world. For more information, visit www.cirm.ca.gov.

  

**Position Summary**

CIRM is seeking a highly organized and experienced Program Manager for Program Development and Operations to support the planning, development, and effective operation of CIRM's scientific programs.

  

Reporting to the Chief Science Officer (CSO), the Program Manager works across CIRM's Programs organization to coordinate program development, improve operational consistency, track major activities and decision points, and identify issues that require attention or resolution. The position works closely with Program Leads, Project Managers and partner functions, including Review, Grants Management, Legal, Finance, Communications, and IT/Software Development.

  

The Program Manager provides operational management and direction within established processes and, in coordination with the CSO identifies where new or improved processes are needed and supports their development and implementation. The position maintains an integrated view across program areas, identifies gaps and dependencies, brings issues forward early, and helps ensure decisions are translated into clear actions and follow-through.

  

This role requires someone who can work across multiple teams, make sense of complex and sometimes competing priorities, and bring structure and clarity without adding unnecessary process.

  

**Job Functions**

Program Development and Funding Cycle Coordination

* Coordinate the development and implementation of new and revised funding programs, working across Program teams, Review, Grants Management, Legal, Communications, and other functions.
* Maintain visibility across major funding-cycle activities and decision points, including concept development, eligibility, application review, programmatic recommendations, governance review, launch, and implementation.
* Coordinate timelines, dependencies, responsibilities, and required inputs across functions. Identify gaps or potential delays early and work with responsible teams to resolve them.
* Support the development of Program concepts, Program Announcements (PAs), Request for Applications (RFAs), amendments, implementation plans, and related materials, while ensuring primary content ownership remains with the appropriate Program and functional teams.
* Coordinate operational readiness for Executive Team, Science Subcommittee, Board, and other governance review of Programs activities, ensuring materials, recommendations, timelines, and required decisions are clear and appropriately coordinated.
* Track significant decisions through implementation and coordinate resulting actions, timelines, and operational changes.
* In coordination with Program Manager (Strategy and Operations) responsible for tracking outcomes of CIRM funding, aggregating to CSO and incorporating it back into funding cycles where needed.

  

Cross-Program Operations

* Maintain an integrated view of major priorities, timelines, dependencies, and operational risks across Discovery and Education, Preclinical Development, Clinical Development and other Programs activities as they relate to funding cycles.
* Work with Program Leads and PMs to identify operational gaps, clarify responsibilities, improve coordination, and support timely execution.
* Identify issues that require CSO attention and provide summaries of the issue, implications, recommended next steps, and decisions needed.
* At the direction of the CSO and in coordination with Program Leads, develop and implement operational expectations and common practices across Programs.
* Identify operational risks, cross-functional dependencies, unclear ownership, and process gaps related to funding cycles; work with responsible teams to identify options and resolve issues, and bring significant or unresolved matters to the CSO early with recommended next steps.
* Track agreed actions and decisions through implementation, particularly where responsibilities cross Programs or organizational functions.

  

Operational Planning and Process Improvement

* Assess how funding cycle efforts are being carried out across Programs and identify practical opportunities to improve consistency, efficiency, accountability, and visibility.
* Develop and maintain appropriate operating tools for funding cycles, including integrated plans, dashboards (excluding Review cycle trackers), decision and action trackers, templates, SOPs, and common workflows.
* Help distinguish between funding cycle processes that should be standardized across Programs and those that appropriately remain specific to individual program areas.
* Support implementation of agreed funding cycle process changes and assess whether they are working as intended.

  

Organizational Visibility and Planning

**The Office of the City Administrator**includes 20+ agencies and over 1,000 dedicated staff who provide essential services to San Francisco residents and businesses and improve the administration of government.  
  
**Our Mission**  
The City Administrator’s Office is strongly committed to ensuring efficient and effective government services, increasing the City’s safety and resiliency, strengthening the local economy, supporting equity and inclusion, and optimizing the City’s capital planning and infrastructure.

**Our Vision**

We are committed to ensuring that the City's services are inclusive, efficient, equitable, and culturally competent for San Franciscans of all races, ethnic backgrounds, religions, and sexual orientations. The Government Operations Initiative (GovOps) brings together teams across the City Administrator’s Office, Controller’s Office, and Department of Human Resources to tackle complex operational challenges that cut across traditional departmental boundaries. GovOps teams combine project management, policy and process expertise, data analysis, and change management to develop and implement complex reforms. Our work requires understanding how City processes operate today, identifying where they create unnecessary burden or barriers, and partnering across departments to design and implement practical improvements.

**The Procurement Reform Team**

The Senior Project Manager will join the GovOps Procurement Reform team within the City Administrator’s Office. Our team leads citywide efforts to make procurement and contracting simpler, faster, more effective, and more accessible for both the City staff who use these processes and the suppliers who do business with the City.

Our portfolio spans policy and legislative reform, business process redesign, technology modernization, data and performance, and improvements to the supplier experience. * How can we make City processes simpler and more effective without losing the safeguards necessary for responsible stewardship of public resources?
* How can we reduce barriers for small and local businesses, community-based organizations, and other suppliers seeking to do business with the City?
* How do we design reforms that are ambitious enough to meaningfully improve government while also being practical, sustainable, and responsive to the people who will use them?

We are looking for someone who is committed to ensuring that public institutions serve communities equitably and sees themselves as a public-sector leader.

The Senior Project Manager will report to the Deputy Director of Operations and Procurement Reform in the Office of Contract Administration.

new_jobs.description:
For People is improving government digital services for the disadvantaged population. We work directly with government agencies to modernize software, systems, and platforms so that they better serve people.

**Your Impact**
---------------

Every month, hundreds of thousands of people go looking for facts about Medicare and Medicaid. They are researchers, reporters, policy staff, and health care providers. When the data is hard to find, a file is too large to post, or a column quietly changes its name between releases, their work slows down or goes wrong.

This project supports the website where the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publishes that data for the public. It hosts a large catalog of datasets, lookup tools, and dashboards from across the agency, available for download, as interactive tools, and via a public API. As Program Manager, you will lead the team that builds and runs it. This is a hands-on role. You’ll facilitate partner meetings, support the team when they are blocked, and get into project details as needed to report clearly on the team’s progress. You’ll work elbow-to-elbow with the project’s technical and product leadership. You will learn about the work enough to identify and help mitigate delivery risks and hold the team accountable for what we promise to government partners.

This position is a full-time position **contingent** on For People being awarded a federal contract. If awarded, this position’s expected start date is February 2027.

**Our Culture**
---------------

For People is a team of humans. We place a significant amount of emphasis on positive work-life balance, setting healthy expectations, and making sure our loved ones are taken care of first. That means picking a child up from school during the day or going for a mid-day walk is okay!

This position is ***100% remote***. Our entire team is remote across the United States, from the West Coast to the East Coast. There will never be a return-to-office, as we have none! Occasional travel to CMS headquarters in Baltimore, MD (2-3 times per year) is required. These trips are infrequent and scheduled well in advance.

This full-time position's published base salary range is between **$100,000 and $160,000** annually. This band ranges across both the Program Manager and Senior Program Manager pay band, which will be determined based on relevant experience. All positions include generous benefits (e.g., For People pays 100% of Gold-tier employee health insurance premiums) and annual company profit sharing.

**Your Opportunities**
----------------------

On this project, you will be the delivery lead on a cross-functional team of about 15 people spanning engineering, design, user research, and support functions. The team may expand to up to 25 members in the future. As the Program Manager, you will:

* Build a collaborative and trusting team culture across all disciplines in the program
* Run agile practices including sprints, planning cycles, demos, and retrospectives, all of which include CMS stakeholders
* Coordinate with CMS offices that publish data on the public portal; share progress transparently and build positive working relationships with partner contracting teams
* Proactively identify and mitigate risks to project delivery
* Keep the program in line with contract, security, and accessibility requirements, including Section 508 and the site's Authority to Operate (ATO)
* Report status and outcomes to CMS and For People leadership, using live dashboards wherever possible and finding efficiency gains through automation
* Lead the handoff from the current contractor in your first few months so users see no disruption

**You Bring**
-------------

* A humble and caring attitude aligning with For People’s values: passion, fun, curiosity, sustainability, humility, and respect
* 8+ years of relevant experience in program or project management, including managing government contracts
* Degree in management, public administration, information technology, or a related field
* Experience with open data projects
* Experience managing cross-functional teams, with the ability to lead teams of 15 to 25 people as the contract grows
* Deep knowledge of agile product management principles
* Familiarity with collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, Slack, and GitHub
* Ability to oversee all aspects of task order management including reporting, sprint planning, and project planning
* Experience facilitating stakeholder engagement across multiple government agency offices and data owners

**It Would Be Great If You Also Have**
--------------------------------------

* Experience working directly with CMS programs or data
* Experience with public websites built on Drupal
* Experience leading a contract transition from an incumbent team

**Some Fine Print**
-------------------

You will be working on a United States government platform, and they have a few basic requirements for contractors like ourselves. All work must be physically performed within the United States at all times. In addition, you must be a United States citizen and be able to pass a government-performed public trust background check.  
  
For People is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, and/or veteran status.

Program Manager
  
  
***Location:***  
Princeton, NJ or Los Angeles, CA (currently hybrid) - 2 days per week in the office. Must be local to one of our offices, others will not be considered.  
  
***Reports To:***  
Director, Program Management
  
  
***Salary Range:***  
$80,000 – $120,000. Exact compensation will vary based on experience  
  
***Other:***  
Vaccination against COVID-19 is a prerequisite for employment at CHDI Management  
  
***About CHDI Foundation, Inc.***  
CHDI Foundation, Inc. is a privately funded nonprofit biomedical research organization exclusively dedicated to collaboratively developing therapeutics that will substantially improve the lives of those affected by Huntington’s disease (HD). Our scientists work closely with a network of more than 700 researchers in academic and industrial laboratories around the world in the pursuit of these novel therapies, providing strategic scientific direction to ensure that our common goals remain in focus. This helps bridge the translational gap that often exists between academic and industrial research pursuits and that adds costly delays to therapy development. In its role as a collaborative enabler, CHDI seeks to bring the right partners together to identify and address critical scientific issues and move drug candidates to clinical evaluation as rapidly as possible. Our activities extend from exploratory biology to the identification and validation of therapeutic targets, and from drug discovery and development to clinical studies and trials. More information about CHDI can be found at www.chdifoundation.org.  
  
***Job Description:***  
We are seeking a highly motivated and organized Program Manager to join the preclinical Program Management Office supporting various preclinical teams. The candidate should have strong experience in the coordination and management of translational and preclinical studies. In addition, the candidate should be very detail-oriented and have significant experience working with Ph.D. level scientists. The position offers significant growth opportunities, exposure to a new model of non-profit orphan disease drug discovery, and an entrepreneurial work environment with high impact.
  
  
***Job Responsibilities:***

* Work with CHDI Science Directors to understand project goals and deliverables in order to enable the execution of legal contracts with collaborators, including fee-for-service companies, academic institutions, pharmaceutical companies and biotechnology companies.
* Work with CHDI’s finance and legal officers to execute contracts in compliance with Foundation policies.
* Work with scientists and the financial officer to evaluate and optimize proposed budgets for new projects.
* Use existing tracking tools to monitor the progress of executed contracts in accordance with the terms specified in each contract.
* Identify and communicate potential issues and delays to scientists, the legal department and the financial officer in a timely manner and propose solutions to remedy the issues in an expedited fashion.
* Liaise with collaborative counterparts to ensure: a) that studies are conducted in accordance with corresponding contracts; and b) that deliverables are delivered on time and per allocated funds to each such study.
* Work with materials/data repository managers to ensure: a) that materials/data are available and can be provided for a given study prior to the execution of contracts; and b) that materials/data generated by collaborators are properly registered in CHDI’s databases, consequently tracked and deposited.
* Participate and host internal and external meetings as needed, prepare meeting minutes, follow up on action items and act in an ‘advisory’ role on matters related to operations, finances and legal issues.
* Ensure all post-execution contract management requirements are performed including invoicing, audit reports, material shipments, amendments, and contract close-outs.
* Review periodic invoices, ensuring they align with financial terms of corresponding contracts and CHDI policy, flag discrepancies and resolve issues with collaborators and/or the CHDI financial officer in an expedited fashion to meet the monthly timeline.
* Review academic financial audit reports and reconcile any discrepancies. Work with principal investigators and grant analysts at academic institutions to understand and resolve budgetary discrepancies.
* File scientific reports and project management documents in CHDI’s document management system and distribute internally to relevant individuals.
* Prepare and summarize contract budgetary information to support annual fiscal year forecasting.
* As required, work with scientific team leads to track team Goals, Strategies, and Objectives in existing tracking tools, ensuring updates to project status and resources.
* Participate in monthly Program Managers’ team meetings and host selected meetings in accordance with the pre-established schedule.
* Propose tools and strategies to streamline and optimize tracking of studies and expenditures whenever possible.

  
***Job requirements:***

* Bachelors or Masters Degree in life sciences or chemical sciences.
* Contract management experience and hands-on experience coordinating studies with collaborating sites.
* Experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
* Experience in licensing, technology transfer and alliance management in industry or academia a plus.

* Strong organizational and multitasking skills.
* Superior written and oral communication skills.
* Highly proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.

Curiosity about AI and emerging technologies and their application to data and investment research

* Proficiency in Microsoft Excel
* Superb business intuition and a solution-oriented, methodical approach to problem-solving
* Ability to collaborate and build relationships across multiple business units within the firm

* Define and maintain strategic product visions, multi-year roadmaps and investment priorities for enterprise technology products and platforms.
* Serve as Product Owner for assigned technology products, guiding lifecycle strategy, modernization and ongoing enhancement.
* Develop, refine and prioritize product backlogs based on business value, risk, operational requirements and available funding.
* Translate business objectives into actionable product requirements, epics, user stories and acceptance criteria.
* Lead large-scale technology programs spanning multiple projects, teams, vendors and business functions.
* Develop program strategies, investment roadmaps, delivery schedules, milestones and governance structures.
* Coordinate digital transformation, infrastructure modernization, cloud migration, application modernization and technology lifecycle initiatives.
* Manage competing priorities and dependencies across product, engineering, architecture, cybersecurity, infrastructure and operations teams.
* Establish quarterly and annual planning processes that align technology delivery with business and enterprise IT priorities.
* Develop and manage portfolio budgets, forecasts, funding plans and resource allocations.
* Prepare business cases, financial justifications and investment recommendations for executive leadership.
* Track portfolio financial performance, spending, benefits realization and return on technology investments.
* Manage vendor relationships, technology contracts, managed service providers and service performance expectations.
* Establish product KPIs, service metrics, adoption measurements and operational performance indicators.
* Monitor program health, risks, issues, dependencies, delivery performance and strategic outcomes.
* Lead executive reviews, steering committee discussions, governance meetings and strategic planning sessions.
* Develop executive dashboards, portfolio reports, investment summaries and strategic recommendations.
* Coordinate delivery from initial planning and design through implementation, adoption and operational transition.
* Apply Agile, Scrum, Hybrid or Waterfall delivery approaches based on program complexity and organizational requirements.
* Identify and resolve organizational barriers, resource constraints, delivery risks and competing stakeholder priorities.
* Lead technology refresh, technical debt reduction, lifecycle management and operational improvement initiatives.
* Partner with cybersecurity, architecture and compliance teams to ensure technology solutions meet enterprise security and governance requirements.
* Mentor Program Managers, Project Managers, Scrum Masters, Product Owners and other technology delivery professionals.
* Drive organizational change, stakeholder adoption and continuous improvement across enterprise technology programs.
